title: Priority basket: Even-key census
summary: Insert all readings into a binary min-heap and repeatedly remove the smallest. Produce that removal sequence, preserving duplicates. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values.
descriptionMd:
A heap-shaped basket keeps the smallest numbered service ticket ready at its opening. Neri separates readings for the office's even-numbered keys. A zero reading belongs in that count, just like any other even number.

Insert all readings into a binary min-heap and repeatedly remove the smallest. Produce that removal sequence, preserving duplicates.

Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values.

Implement priorityBasketEvenKeyCensus(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Binary heaps. Insert all readings into a binary min-heap and repeatedly remove the smallest. Produce that removal sequence, preserving duplicates. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n log n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with binary heaps. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

Insert all readings into a binary min-heap and repeatedly remove the smallest. Produce that removal sequence, preserving duplicates. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [-3,0,7,7,12]. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. This gives 2.
The derived sequence is [-2,4,4,4]. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. This gives 4.
The derived sequence is []. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. This gives 0.
